Hi Laura — great to hear. We can definitely run two regional sessions the week of Mar 23. A couple of scheduling notes:

- US already moved to daylight time on Mar 8; EU switches later in March (there's a common off-week where local times don't align). That causes confusion for calendar invites that display local times differently depending on recipients' calendars.
- To avoid invites that flip by an hour for some participants, we usually either: (a) create two separate invites (EMEA/APAC + Americas) with clear local-time labels, or (b) run one global session at an awkward hour and record for APAC follow-up.

Proposed approach: two 45-minute sessions (EMEA/APAC and AMER). Marcus and I can lead each; Hannah will join for the technical Q&A. I'm attaching a short agenda and a tentative .ics with both placeholders — please confirm which regional slot you'd like us to lock.

Suggested slots (local display):
- EMEA/APAC: Tue, Mar 24, 10:00–10:45 GMT / Wed, Mar 25 19:00 AEDT
- AMER: Wed, Mar 25, 10:30–11:15 PDT / Wed, Mar 25, 13:30–14:15 EDT

If BrightBank prefers a single consolidated session, we can offer a "canary" quick test invite first to ensure everyone's calendar shows the correct local time.

Thanks — attaching: RDW-Agenda-Regional-Demo.pdf, regional-demo-slots.ics

—
Soojin Lee\| Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Looping in Hannah — quick note from ops: when we send the two invites, add the region name to the summary (e.g., "BrightBank – Demo (EMEA/APAC)" and "BrightBank – Demo (AMERICAS)") and include the timezone in the description. I've seen Outlook/Exchange users in some banks show the wrong offset if the invite is ambiguous during DST transition weeks.

Also recommend we:
- Lock speaker list so we don't shuffle presenters between sessions.
- Publish a 10-minute recording right after the first session for any cross-region stakeholders considering attending the second.

If Laura confirms the EMEA slot, I'll own the materials for the AMER run and coordinate the recording link.

-Marcus
